thread.title: Crowding In A Few Names To Close 2018

author: The Idea Guide
title: Crowding In A Few Names To Close 2018
text:
by Daniel Shvartsman
It's been two weeks since I wrote a survey review of the long and short ideas we've published on Seeking Alpha. One change in the vantage point from looking at two weeks of articles vs. one is that patterns stand out more clearly. The popular names always have a lot of coverage - your Microns ( MU ), your General Electrics ( GE ), your Apples ( AAPL ) - but there are other names that stand out when you consider publication over a longer time horizon.
On the long side for these two weeks, I'm going to dwell on a few of these names. On the short side, there's a little less crowding (beyond the usual), but a few interesting ideas have popped up. So let's get into them.
Long Ideas We published 431 long ideas over the past two weeks. Let's get to some of the clusters that stand out:
Exxon Mobil Riding Guyana Oil Boom Higher by Callum Turcan Exxon Mobil: This Dividend Aristocrat Is Undervalued And Yields Over 4% by Steven Fiorillo Exxon Mobil Bets Big On Permian Bonanza by Callum Turcan Exxon Mobil ( XOM ) is hardly under the radar, but it gets taken for granted. It's one of the oil majors, oil is in a downturn, and it's a steady dividend payer (even managing to grow its dividend through the 2014-15 period). So it doesn't come to my attention often.
Callum Turcan wrote about it twice in December, focusing on two different areas where Exxon might expand production - Guyana and the Permian basin. It's a reminder of the capital intensity of the oil business. Steven Fiorillo then comes in with a fuller take on the company's financial and operating position. I'm not sure I agree with every comment - the company has net debt of $39B, for example, which is not trivial - but it does paint a rosy picture for XOM. Since the financial crisis, the stock has basically returned just the dividend, and it would be helpful to see a little bit more on how the current oil climate may be affecting its cash flows going forward.
Sentiment Check - It's been a long time since anyone pitched a short XOM thesis on SA. Commentary is mostly bullish, though there are a few skeptics about oil in the SA ecosystem.
Palo Alto Networks: The 2 Core Reasons I'm Staying Long by DoctoRx Palo Alto Networks: Pay No Mind To The Market And Keep Buying by Gary Alexander Palo Alto: Some Concerns Despite Excellent Q1 2019 Results by Herve Blandin Before reviewing the work on Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ), I want to point out that the stock is up 27% for the year but fell into a bear market in September/October. Which is to say, conversations around price action can be really silly. (I am guilty of perpetuating these conversations though).
PANW is a popular 'looks like a GARP but has an even more reasonable multiple' tech name. It trades at 17.5x TTM free cash flow, which is not bad. Interestingly, DoctoRx's bet is all about management - Nikesh Arora as the new CEO and the company's co-founders rejoining the fray are the bullish indicators for his thesis. Gary Alexander points to accelerating revenue growth, and 31% year over year revenue growth at a 17.5x multiple is pretty impressive. Herve Blandin meanwhile says the fundamentals are good, but EV/Sales is high and the company's share based compensation puts a drag on numbers. (DoctoRx does some good digging into the components of the SBC, for what it's worth).
All in all, this does look intriguing. GAAP losses are not exciting, and I suspect cash flow is supported by share based compensation dropping back into the numbers, but strong growth in a sector - cybersecurity - that would seem to still have importance is nothing to sniff at.
Sentiment Check - There are a few skeptics out there about PANW's competitive positioning, but most commenters I see are bullish the stock. It's been a long time since anyone has pitched this as a short as well.
Skyworks Solutions: Cheap, Very Cheap by ChartMasterPro Skyworks Is A Mini Texas Instruments, But Much Cheaper by Shareholders Unite Skyworks: Should You Ride Out The Storm? by Kumquat Research Skyworks Is Our Preferred 5G And IoT Investment Idea by WideAlpha Skyworks ( SWKS ) is a chip provider, primarily for cell phones. So it trades heavily off of Apple's news and to a lesser degree Samsung's ( OTC:SSNLF ). I owned the name for some time earlier this decade and found the company to be a consistent beat and raise play, but also tethered to whatever was going on with Apple as a stock - Apple accounted for 47% of SWKS' FY 2018 revenue.
These four articles present a full picture on the bullish outlook for SWKS. ChartMasterPro focuses on the (attractive) numbers. That's good as a backdrop - less than 14x free cash flow for a company growing operating income is not bad - but that leaves one hunting for reasons. Kumquat Research points out the two biggies - slowing cell phone demand in China, and slowing Apple unit growth. On the flipside, there's opportunities in 5G and IoT, as three of these authors mention.
The company is buying back shares aggressively, has a 2% dividend yield, trades for the aforementioned reasonable multiple, and has no debt. So there's a lot to attract investors. The Apple reliance is a real issue, though, and not just because of any vulnerability to Apple - SWKS has long talked about growing out of its reliance on high-end cell phones, but Apple's share of revenue is higher than at any point since the beginning of the decade (I would guess it's at an all-time high). At what point do other revenue sources really scale up? And if that's not coming soon, how much does it make sense to buy SWKS instead of Apple itself?
Sentiment Check - Drifting into these somewhat less followed names, I find less contention. There are a few people calling out the Apple reliance, and there's some good discussion about Qorvo ( QRVO ) and its competitive challenge. But not a lot of flat out negative sentiment.
A few other headlines that caught my eye, though I won't be able to review them more closely here:
GTT Communications: Substantial Upside For A Misunderstood Telecom Company by Buckley Capital Management PYS: The Biggest Arbitrage In Fixed Income At The Moment by Arbitrage Trader Cheap Assets And Big Upside At SandRidge by ASB Capital Short ideas We published 24 short ideas over the past two weeks, which is not a huge number. Tesla ( TSLA ) only shows up three times, which is marks a bear market in Tesla short ideas (# of short ideas still up big year to date!). Three ideas worth spending time with:
Veeva: An Asymmetric Short by Akram's Razor Akram's Razor has covered Veeva ( VEEV ) well in the past. He does a deep dive into the competitive landscape here, but the thesis is pretty simple:
Iqvia ( IQV ) is competing with Veeva and starting to win major pharmaceutical companies' business. Veeva is still very reliant on Salesforce.com ( CRM ) Veeva trades very expensively, even compared to CRM. Together, this puts Veeva in a hard place, where a 16.5x EV/Sales multiple might come in for a correction.
Sentiment Check - Very good discussion on a few points, with a mix of sentiment in the comment stream. We've published a few long ideas this year, with no one coming out short since Vince Martin wrote it up in late 2015. Incidentally and maybe not coincidentally, Citron Research came out short VEEV on Tuesday, a couple days after this idea appeared on Akram's Razor's marketplace service.
Adient Plc's Bargain Price Doesn't Make It Worth The Risk by Centaur Investments Centaur downgrades their view on Adient ( ADNT ) from hold to sell/short, even as the stock plumbs new 52-week lows. I think this makes sense, actually, as there is something to the broken axle concept. And I'm afraid I got to this late, as Centaur's price target has already been reached.
ADNT is an auto seats supplier (not great, Bob), and was spun out of Johnson Controls ( JCI ) two years ago. It suspended its dividend and took a large impairment. It has $2.7B of net debt on its balance sheet and produced $312M in free cash flow the last two years combined (less this year than in 2017). That's not a great set-up. The company has a term loan worth $1.2B due in 2021, and then maturities in 2024 and 2026 with relatively low coupons (under 5%). So it could be worse.
Centaur projects positive free cash flow by 2020 and gets to a $19 price target through that, just above where we are now. But between the term loan, the cyclical challenges, and a number of local issues that Centaur points out, ADNT does seem to be in a rough spot. So I might add that while it reached Centaur's target, this looks like a situation to consider from the short side more than the long side.
Sentiment Check - There is some bullishness in the comment stream, and we've had a couple other authors pitch ADNT over the course of this year as a long.
Loop Industries' Problems Are More Than Plastic by Aaron Chow Aaron Chow is a new contributor to SA, and his first piece is a bit of a doozy. He argues that Loop Industries ( LOOP ), a Quebec-based recycling company, is making their technology out to be more impressive than it really is. If I understand the essence properly, the company claims to be certified to process recycling of certain plastics, and to actively recycle others, but Chow argues that they are not properly certified and that they are not recycling as much as they say. He points out concerns with management and insider and company sales of shares as well. It's an intriguing story because LOOP appears to be pre-revenue , and this is not an obvious industry to find a company like that which also has a $260M+ market cap. This is our first on the company in its four years of trading. Worth having a look.
Sentiment Check - Comments were to a larger degree supportive of the author's work. Like a biotech, this company comes with a lot of hope given how important recycling/cleaning up plastic is, and that is expressed in the comments as well.
Other ideas that I want to flag for your attention:
SP Plus Bags Is Too Expensive by Robbert Manders Short IDT Corporation: Unjustified Run-Up, Inflated Revenues, Net Income, Operating Cash Flow, And Broken Business Model by Olsny Freitas ***
That's it for this week's Idea Guide. This is a weekly article for Essential and PRO+ subscribers that normally comes out on Friday. We'll stick to that through the end of the year. Follow this account if you want the article sent out as a full-text email.
If you have any favorite ideas, suggestions, or corrections, comment below or send me a direct message , or email me at daniel@seekingalpha.com . I would love to hear how to make this more useful for you. Have a great weekend.
Disclosure: I/we have no positions in any stocks mentioned, and no plans to initiate any positions within the next 72 hours. I wrote this article myself, and it expresses my own opinions.
